description: Add a dedicated TUI screen for managing wallet metadata -- create wallets explicitly, edit custody type and description, rename wallets (updating all ledger references), toggle active/inactive status, and merge duplicate wallets. Surfaces the wallets table that exists in the schema but has no management interface.
principles: Explicit over Implicit - Wallets should be first-class entities users can manage, not just strings extracted from transactions
Safe Renames - Renaming a wallet updates all ledger rows atomically in a single transaction
No Data Loss - Merge and rename operations preserve all transaction history
Progressive Disclosure - Basic operations (create, edit) are prominent; advanced operations (merge, rename) are accessible but not in the way
Consistent Patterns - Follow established TUI screen patterns (Header, Container, DataTable, Footer)

techStack.pattern: Query Object Pattern - extend WalletQuery with write operations

userStories.title: Add wallet CRUD methods to WalletQuery
acceptanceCriteria: WalletQuery.add_wallet(wallet_id, wallet_type, custody, description=None, notes=None) inserts into wallets table
WalletQuery.update_wallet(wallet_id, **kwargs) updates any combination of wallet_type, custody, description, active, notes
WalletQuery.rename_wallet(old_id, new_id) updates wallets.wallet_id AND all ledger.exchange references in a single database transaction
WalletQuery.merge_wallets(source_id, target_id) updates all ledger rows with source_id to target_id, then deletes the source wallet record
WalletQuery.sync_wallets_from_ledger() creates wallet records for any exchange values in ledger that don't exist in wallets table, using infer_custody_type() for defaults
All methods include appropriate error handling (duplicate wallet_id, missing wallet, etc.)
Unit tests for each method using in-memory SQLite

userStories.title: Wallet Management TUI screen - wallet list with DataTable
acceptanceCriteria: New WalletManagementScreen accessible from main menu via 'W' keybinding
Displays all wallets in a DataTable with columns: Name, Type, Custody, Description, Active, Tx Count
Tx Count column shows number of ledger rows referencing each wallet
Calls sync_wallets_from_ledger() on mount to ensure all transaction-referenced wallets appear
Wallet rows color-coded by custody type (green=self-custodied, yellow=custodial, blue=multisig)
Keybinding 'n' to create new wallet, 'e' to edit selected, 'd' to toggle active/inactive
Test: screen renders with wallet data, correct column count

userStories.title: Create Wallet modal
acceptanceCriteria: ModalScreen with form fields: Name (Input, required), Type (Select: exchange/hardware/software/mobile/paper/other), Custody (Select: self-custodied/custodial/multisig), Description (Input, optional), Notes (Input, optional)
Name field validates: not empty, not already existing (checks wallets table)
On submit, calls WalletQuery.add_wallet() and refreshes the wallet list
On cancel, dismisses without changes
Test: modal creates wallet, validation rejects duplicate name

userStories.title: Edit Wallet modal
acceptanceCriteria: ModalScreen pre-populated with selected wallet's current values
All fields editable except Name (shown as read-only label)
On submit, calls WalletQuery.update_wallet() with changed fields only
Refreshes wallet list on dismiss
Test: modal pre-fills values, update persists to database

userStories.title: Rename Wallet with confirmation
acceptanceCriteria: Keybinding 'r' on selected wallet opens rename modal with Input for new name
Shows warning: 'This will update X transactions in the ledger' (shows actual count)
Confirmation required: user must type the new name twice or click explicit Confirm button
On confirm, calls WalletQuery.rename_wallet() which updates wallets table and all ledger.exchange references atomically
Refreshes wallet list on completion
Test: rename updates wallet_id and all matching ledger.exchange rows

userStories.title: Merge Wallets with confirmation
acceptanceCriteria: Keybinding 'm' on selected wallet opens merge modal
Shows Select dropdown of other wallets to merge INTO (target wallet keeps its name)
Shows summary: 'Merge X transactions from [source] into [target]'
Confirmation required before proceeding
On confirm, calls WalletQuery.merge_wallets() - all source transactions reassigned to target, source wallet record deleted
Refreshes wallet list on completion
Test: merge reassigns all transactions, source wallet removed

userStories.title: Update Getting Started guide and keyboard navigation
acceptanceCriteria: GETTING_STARTED.md keyboard table includes 'W' for Wallet Management
Main menu includes Wallet Management option
Help screen includes wallet management keybindings
Feature-11 summary document completed

high: rename_wallet() and merge_wallets() modify ledger data - must be atomic transactions with rollback on failure
Renaming a wallet used by many transactions could be slow on large databases - consider batch UPDATE
medium: sync_wallets_from_ledger() on screen mount adds a query on every open - should be fast but monitor
Merge operation deletes a wallet record - must confirm source wallet has no special significance
low: New screen follows established TUI patterns
WalletQuery extension follows Query Object pattern from Feature-8
All modal patterns proven in Import Wizard (Feature-9)
